To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the vegetation and insects of the Beringian landscape during the last glaciation and deglaciation indicate that: (1) the Bering Land (and Sea) Bridge was never dominated by steppe; (2) the vegetation was dominated by mesic shrub tundra; (3) the climate was colder than present-day, with a summer climate warmer than present-day on the Chukotka Peninsula and colder than the present-day on the Alaskan North Slope; (4)

the land bridge during the Wisconsin glacial maximum was covered by birch-heaths-graminoid vegetation with ponds and that the vegetation and climate during the late-glacial period were more similar to the present-day than to the present-day.

(1) the land bridge had widespread mesic tundra during the last glaciation, (2) steppe-tundra was absent on the land bridge, and (3) the land bridge was available for human migration until 11,000 years ago.
